patient.name: Douglas Harrington
patient.chief_complaint: Progressive gait imbalance, sensory loss, and hand clumsiness over 3 months — worsening rapidly
patient.hpi: Douglas Harrington is a 66-year-old retired mechanical engineer and former 35 pack-year smoker who quit 12 years ago. He presents with a 3-month history of rapidly progressive sensory ataxia, gait imbalance, and bilateral hand clumsiness that has made him unable to write or button his shirt. His primary care physician performed initial NCS that reportedly showed 'neuropathy' and referred him to neurology for progressive gait difficulty. He describes the onset as bilateral hand and foot numbness occurring simultaneously — not the foot-first, length-dependent pattern he had heard about from a diabetic friend. He notes that his feet and hands feel like they belong to someone else, and he has near-daily falls at home. He has noticed his handwriting has deteriorated dramatically and he cannot perform fine motor tasks. He denies any significant weakness — he can rise from a chair and climb stairs — emphasizing that his problem is 'balance and feeling, not strength.' He denies bowel or bladder dysfunction. He does not have diabetes. He has lost 6 kg unintentionally over the past 4 months, which he initially attributed to reduced appetite. His wife notes he has been more forgetful over the past 6 weeks with occasional word-finding difficulty. He was treated empirically with IVIG 2 g/kg 6 weeks ago by an outside neurologist who suspected CIDP — he reports no improvement. He takes no medications known to cause neuropathy. He has no family history of neuropathy. He has no alcohol history. A chest X-ray obtained incidentally for a 'persistent cough' 5 months ago was read as 'within normal limits' but was not formally reviewed by pulmonology.
pmh: 35 pack-year smoking history, quit 12 years ago
Empirical IVIG 2 g/kg given 6 weeks ago — no clinical improvement
patient.review_of_systems: Positive: bilateral simultaneous hand and foot numbness (non-length-dependent), severe gait imbalance, falls, hand clumsiness, pseudoathetosis (unintentional hand writhing when eyes closed), unintentional 6 kg weight loss, persistent cough 5 months, mild word-finding difficulty. Negative: significant weakness, diplopia, dysphagia, bowel/bladder dysfunction, rash, joint swelling, fever.

medications.drug: Gabapentin 300 mg three times daily (started 8 weeks ago, minimal benefit)

family_history: Father: died at 74, colon cancer. Mother: died at 81, stroke. No family history of neuropathy, no pes cavus.

social_history.note: Retired mechanical engineer. Married. Former smoker 35 pack-years, quit 12 years ago. Non-drinker. No illicit drugs. No toxic occupational exposures. Lives at home with wife.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented x3 (disoriented to date). Mild word-finding difficulty on confrontational naming. Montreal Cognitive Assessment 24/30 (missed 3/5 words on delayed recall, 1 visuospatial task).
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: CN II-XII intact. No facial sensory loss. Mild saccadic pursuit eye movements bilaterally.
neurological_exam.motor: STRENGTH PRESERVED. Hip flexors 5/5, knee extensors 5/5, dorsiflexion 5/5. Upper extremities 5/5 throughout. No significant weakness. Motor power essentially intact — ataxia is sensory, not motor.
neurological_exam.sensory: SEVERE PAN-SENSORY LOSS NON-LENGTH-DEPENDENT. Pinprick: severely reduced all four limbs to mid-forearm and mid-thigh (NOT stocking-glove — involves proximal limbs and trunk). Vibration: ABSENT at all tested sites including knees and elbows (proximal level loss). Proprioception: ABSENT at toes AND fingers bilaterally. Joint position sense absent at ankles and wrists. Light touch: severely reduced all four limbs. Trunk: patchy reduced pinprick over thorax.
neurological_exam.reflexes: DIFFUSELY ABSENT. Achilles: absent bilaterally. Patellar: absent bilaterally. Biceps: absent bilaterally. Triceps: absent bilaterally. Diffuse areflexia with preserved strength — hallmark of sensory neuronopathy (dorsal root ganglion disease).
neurological_exam.coordination: SEVERELY IMPAIRED PROPRIOCEPTIVE ATAXIA. Finger-nose: dysmetric bilaterally due to sensory loss, not cerebellar tremor. Heel-shin: severely impaired. Cannot perform tandem walk. Pseudoathetosis present bilaterally at fingers when eyes closed.
neurological_exam.gait: Severely ataxic, wide-based, stomping gait. Requires bilateral arm support. Positive Romberg — falls immediately on eye closure. Unable to stand on one foot.
neurological_exam.special_tests: Pseudoathetosis: PRESENT bilaterally — involuntary writhing finger movements with eyes closed and arms outstretched (pathognomonic for severe proprioceptive loss from DRG disease). Lhermitte's sign: negative. No muscle tenderness.

results.NCS_interpretation: PAN-SENSORY SNAPS ABSENT IN ALL NERVES TESTED (7/7 absent) WITH COMPLETELY NORMAL MOTOR NCS AND NORMAL EMG. This is the electrodiagnostic hallmark of SENSORY NEURONOPATHY (GANGLIONOPATHY) — dorsal root ganglion (DRG) cell destruction. Normal motor NCS with diffuse SNAP absence definitively excludes peripheral axonal polyneuropathy (which would show at least some residual SNAP amplitude). The pattern is non-length-dependent (upper and lower limbs equally affected). IVIG is ineffective for DRG disease — treatment must target the underlying cause.

followup_outputs.interpretation: Sensory neuronopathy confirmed by NCS: all SNAPs absent bilaterally with preserved motor conduction and normal EMG. This is DRG-level disease, not peripheral axon disease. Causes: paraneoplastic (anti-Hu, SCLC), Sjögren's, idiopathic. In this former smoker with weight loss and SIADH — paraneoplastic anti-Hu is most likely.

followup_outputs.indication: Paraneoplastic panel in CSF; exclude CNS infection or leptomeningeal carcinomatosis
followup_outputs.oligoclonal_bands: PRESENT — 4 bands in CSF, none in serum (intrathecal IgG synthesis)
followup_outputs.paraneoplastic_CSF: Anti-Hu (ANNA-1) detected in CSF by immunofluorescence — POSITIVE
followup_outputs.interpretation: Mild lymphocytic pleocytosis (8 WBC), elevated protein 72 mg/dL, intrathecal oligoclonal IgG synthesis — pattern consistent with paraneoplastic CNS inflammation. Anti-Hu (ANNA-1) POSITIVE in CSF confirms paraneoplastic etiology. No malignant cells in CSF (leptomeningeal carcinomatosis excluded). Combined sensory neuronopathy + limbic encephalitis + anti-Hu = classic Hu syndrome — 80-90% caused by small cell lung cancer.

output.interpretation: Opening pressure: normal. Protein: normal. Glucose: normal.

results.Anti_SSA: Negative (Sjögren's excluded as cause of ganglionopathy)

followup_outputs.interpretation: Anti-Hu (ANNA-1) STRONGLY POSITIVE at 1:1000 in serum. Anti-Hu is an intracellular antibody targeting HuD RNA-binding protein expressed in neurons and small cell lung cancer. Sensitivity for SCLC is 85-90% when anti-Hu is strongly positive. Anti-Yo, anti-Ri, anti-NMDAR all negative. Sjögren's sensory ganglionopathy excluded (anti-SSA negative). Urgent chest imaging required to identify primary tumor.

followup_outputs.indication: Anti-Hu positive — urgent search for small cell lung cancer; prior CXR reportedly normal 5 months ago

findings.Chest: RIGHT HILAR MASS measuring 2.8 x 2.2 cm. Irregular border with speculation. Associated right paratracheal lymphadenopathy (station 2R, 4R — multiple nodes 0.8-1.4 cm). Central location adjacent to right main bronchus. No pleural effusion.
findings.Lung_parenchyma: No additional parenchymal nodules. No ground glass opacities.
findings.Abdomen: Bilateral adrenal glands: RIGHT ADRENAL NODULE 1.1 cm (indeterminate on CT — PET needed). Liver: no focal lesions. Spleen: normal. Retroperitoneum: no lymphadenopathy.
findings.Bones: No lytic or blastic lesions on CT windows

followup_outputs.interpretation: RIGHT HILAR MASS 2.8 cm with mediastinal lymphadenopathy highly suspicious for primary lung malignancy. In the context of anti-Hu positive paraneoplastic syndrome, this is SCLC until proven otherwise. The prior CXR was false-negative (hilar masses may be subtle on CXR). Adrenal nodule requires PET characterization (adrenal metastasis vs adenoma). Bronchoscopy with biopsy required urgently.

followup_outputs.indication: Tissue diagnosis of right hilar mass; staging for suspected SCLC

findings.Bronchoscopy: Right main bronchus: extrinsic compression from hilar mass. Endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS)-guided biopsy of right hilar mass and station 4R lymph node performed.
findings.Bronchoscopy_biopsy_pathology: SMALL CELL LUNG CARCINOMA (SCLC). Small cells with scant cytoplasm, salt-and-pepper chromatin, nuclear molding. Ki-67 >80% (high proliferative rate). IHC: synaptophysin positive, chromogranin positive, CD56 positive, TTF-1 positive, CK7 positive. CK20 negative. Consistent with primary pulmonary SCLC.
findings.PET_CT: Right hilar mass: SUVmax 18.4 (highly metabolically active). Right paratracheal lymph nodes: SUVmax 8-12 (involved). Right adrenal nodule: SUVmax 4.2 (ADRENAL METASTASIS — extensive stage). Brain PET: SUVmax at right parietal cortex 3.8 (subtle — needs MRI correlation). Bone: no osseous metastases on PET.
findings.Staging: EXTENSIVE STAGE SCLC (adrenal metastasis = M1b). TNM: cT2N2M1b.

followup_outputs.interpretation: Small cell lung carcinoma confirmed on biopsy. Extensive stage (adrenal metastasis). Anti-Hu paraneoplastic syndrome is confirmed — sensory neuronopathy + limbic encephalitis caused by immune response to HuD antigen expressed by SCLC. Paraneoplastic neurological syndromes frequently precede SCLC diagnosis by months (hence prior 'normal' CXR). Immunotherapy for neuropathy is secondary to cancer treatment.

results.title: Paraneoplastic neurological syndromes in patients with small-cell lung cancer: a clinical study
results.journal: Journal of Neurology Neurosurgery and Psychiatry
results.key_finding: Anti-Hu (ANNA-1) is present in 85-90% of paraneoplastic sensory neuronopathy cases. SCLC is the causative tumor in 80% of anti-Hu cases. Neurological symptoms precede tumor diagnosis in 60-80% of cases. NCS shows pan-sensory SNAP loss with preserved motor conduction — electrodiagnostic hallmark of DRG disease.

results.title: Sensory neuronopathy: spectrum of causes, clinical features, and diagnostic approach
results.key_finding: Sensory neuronopathy causes: paraneoplastic (anti-Hu, 35%), Sjögren's (25%), idiopathic (30%), others. Key NCS feature: ALL SNAPs absent with normal motor NCS — distinguishes from polyneuropathy. IVIG is ineffective for paraneoplastic sensory neuronopathy. Tumor treatment may stabilize but rarely improves neurological deficit.

results.title: Immunotherapy for paraneoplastic neurological syndromes: systematic review
results.key_finding: For anti-Hu syndrome: tumor treatment (chemotherapy for SCLC) is primary intervention. Plasma exchange, IVIG, and rituximab have limited benefit for intracellular antigen-mediated PNS (anti-Hu, anti-Yo). Unlike surface antigen syndromes (NMDAR, LGI1), immunotherapy response is poor. Neurological prognosis poor regardless of treatment — DRG neurons do not regenerate.

interactions.description: CRITICAL: Checkpoint inhibitors (atezolizumab, pembrolizumab) are standard in SCLC but may WORSEN paraneoplastic neurological syndromes by amplifying anti-tumor immune response that cross-reacts with neuronal antigens. Published cases of severe worsening of anti-Hu sensory neuronopathy with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors. Oncology and neurology co-management essential. Risk-benefit discussion required — some centers use with careful monitoring, others defer immunotherapy in established PNS.
Both have renal elimination. Monitor renal function. Carboplatin dose based on Calvert formula (AUC x [GFR + 25]). Gabapentin dose adequate at current eGFR 82.

followup_outputs.contraindications: No absolute contraindications to carboplatin-etoposide. Checkpoint inhibitor use requires neurology co-management given established paraneoplastic syndrome.
followup_outputs.recommendations: Oncology-neurology joint management. Proceed with carboplatin-etoposide SCLC treatment. Atezolizumab use requires informed discussion of PNS worsening risk. Prophylactic cranial irradiation decision after chemotherapy response.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Anti-Hu paraneoplastic sensory neuronopathy and limbic encephalitis caused by extensive-stage small cell lung carcinoma
key_findings: Pan-sensory SNAPs absent in all 7 tested nerves with COMPLETELY NORMAL motor NCS and NORMAL EMG — pathognomonic sensory neuronopathy pattern (DRG disease)
Pseudoathetosis bilateral — involuntary finger writhing with eyes closed (severe proprioceptive loss from DRG destruction)
Anti-Hu (ANNA-1) positive serum 1:1000 and CSF — paraneoplastic cause confirmed
Bilateral medial temporal lobe T2/FLAIR signal on brain MRI — paraneoplastic limbic encephalitis
Right hilar mass 2.8 cm on CT chest (CXR was falsely negative 5 months prior)
SCLC confirmed on EBUS biopsy: synaptophysin+, chromogranin+, Ki-67 >80%
Extensive stage: right adrenal metastasis (SUVmax 4.2 on PET)
SIADH (Na 130, urine Na 48, urine osm 484) — paraneoplastic ADH secretion by SCLC
IVIG failure 6 weeks prior — confirms this is NOT CIDP (paraneoplastic sensory neuronopathy is IVIG-refractory)
35 pack-year smoking history — key risk factor
critical_actions: Obtain serum anti-Hu (ANNA-1), anti-Yo, anti-Ri, anti-CRMP5 urgently when sensory neuronopathy is confirmed
CT chest-abdomen-pelvis with contrast urgently (prior CXR insufficient — SCLC hilar masses missed on CXR)
EBUS-guided biopsy of hilar mass for tissue confirmation and SCLC histology
PET-CT for staging (extensive vs limited SCLC determines treatment)
Oncology referral: carboplatin-etoposide chemotherapy ± atezolizumab (with neurology co-management)
Neurology co-management: treat SIADH (fluid restriction, tolvaptan if severe); gabapentin/pregabalin for neuropathic pain
Do NOT re-treat with IVIG — ineffective for paraneoplastic (intracellular antigen) syndromes
Neurology-oncology co-management for checkpoint inhibitor decision in established PNS
pitfalls: Diagnosing CIDP based on elevated CSF protein (paraneoplastic also raises CSF protein with pleocytosis) — NCS pattern discriminates
Treating with IVIG when NCS shows pan-SNAP absence with normal motor — this is DRG disease, not demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy
Trusting normal CXR — SCLC hilar masses are frequently missed on CXR, CT chest is required
Missing the non-length-dependent pattern — upper and lower limbs equally affected simultaneously means DRG disease, not axonal dying back
Failing to obtain paraneoplastic antibody panel in an older male smoker with rapidly progressive sensory neuropathy
Missing limbic encephalitis on brain MRI — medial temporal T2 signal in this context = paraneoplastic (not herpes, not stroke)
Overlooking SIADH as a paraneoplastic clue — SCLC secretes ADH; hyponatremia in a neuropathy patient should trigger malignancy workup
Using checkpoint inhibitors without neurology co-management — may severely worsen anti-Hu paraneoplastic syndrome

optimal_actions.action: interpret_labs (CBC, CMP with Na for SIADH, HbA1c, SPEP, paraneoplastic antibody panel serum)
interpret_labs (NCS/EMG — pan-SNAP absence with normal motor is pathognomonic)
analyze_csf (lymphocytic pleocytosis + elevated protein + oligoclonal bands + anti-Hu CSF)
order_ct_scan (CT chest-abdomen-pelvis — identify SCLC hilar mass missed on CXR)
check_drug_interactions (checkpoint inhibitor caution in paraneoplastic syndrome)

teaching_points: Sensory neuronopathy = pan-SNAP absence with NORMAL motor NCS + NORMAL EMG — this pattern means DRG cell body destruction, not axon disease
Non-length-dependent pattern (upper + lower limbs simultaneously, proximal = distal) distinguishes DRG disease from dying-back axonopathy
Pseudoathetosis (involuntary finger writhing with eyes closed) is pathognomonic for severe proprioceptive loss from DRG disease
Anti-Hu paraneoplastic sensory neuronopathy is caused by SCLC in 80-90% of cases — always obtain CT chest in smokers with this syndrome
CXR has poor sensitivity for SCLC hilar masses — neurological diagnosis should trigger CT chest regardless of CXR result
IVIG is ineffective for intracellular antigen paraneoplastic syndromes (anti-Hu, anti-Yo) — unlike surface antigen syndromes (NMDAR, LGI1) which respond to immunotherapy
SIADH in a neuropathy patient should trigger malignancy workup — SCLC secretes ADH ectopically
Checkpoint inhibitors may worsen established paraneoplastic neurological syndromes — neurology-oncology co-management essential
